title: Lexical-Compat Graph and Marshalling Runbook for Tool/Legacy Function Interop
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers are sending a mix of OpenAI-style "tools" and older "function" invocation payloads. The runtime currently has multiple ad-hoc heuristics leading to inconsistent routing, name collisions, and surprising structured-output shapes during streaming. This ticket defines a deterministic, auditable lexical compatibility graph plus a marshalling runbook to translate and route requests between OpenAI-style tool metadata and our legacy function surface. Goal: ship a low-risk, feature-flagged runtime bridge that resolves tool/function names, preserves call provenance, supports streaming responses and structured outputs, and emits telemetry so we can validate rollouts and detect regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic name-resolution: given a request with tool metadata or legacy function metadata, runtime resolves to a single canonical handler key or emits a clear resolution error
Preserve provenance: response metadata contains original invocation type (openai_tool | legacy_fn), original name, and resolved canonical_name
Streaming compatibility: streaming tool outputs and legacy function responses both support chunked JSON envelope and final structured output validated against declared schema
Collision policy: documented resolution strategy for ambiguous names (namespace priority, alias table, and explicit disambiguation header), implemented and tested
Telemetry: metrics for resolution path, fallback rate, name collisions, stream-close vs final-output mismatch, and per-canonical-handler latency and error counts
Feature flagged rollout with canary: bridge can be enabled per-customer and per-region for progressive deployment
implementation_notes: Introduce a Lexical-Compat Graph (LCG): a lightweight, versioned mapping from observed tool/function names and signatures to a canonical handler id. Stored as JSON manifest in S3 + runtime cache. Example entry: {"canonical":"search.v2", "aliases":["web_search", "Search"], "sig_hash":"sha256:...", "compat_level":"legacy"}

Resolution algorithm (runtime): 1) exact namespace match; 2) alias lookup in LCG; 3) signature-hash match if provided; 4) heuristic fuzzy match with score threshold; 5) fail with 400 and resolution suggestions. Heuristic path is gated and only enabled via flag for now.

Marshalling layer: when a match is found, wrap incoming payload into a canonical invocation envelope: {"canonical_name":..., "invocation_origin": (openai_tool|legacy_fn), "original_name":..., "meta": {source_headers}, "payload": ...}. This preserves original data and ensures downstream handlers see a consistent contract.

Streaming design: use chunked envelope frames with type field (partial, final, error). For streaming OpenAI-style tool outputs that previously emitted text frames, produce 'partial' frames that contain either raw text or a mini-JSON object when structured output is emitted incrementally. Ensure final 'final' frame contains serialized structured output validated against the handler schema. For legacy functions that returned synchronous JSON, runtime will emit a single final frame wrapping the original JSON.

Structured outputs: handler manifests can declare an output schema (JSON Schema draft-07). Runtime validates final output against schema on the hot path in debug/canary mode and logs schema-violation events. Violations in canary cause the invocation to return a safe fallback response (500 with structured diagnostics) and create an alert.

Collision resolution policy: priority order—explicit namespace in client request > exact-case sensitive match > alias table > signature match > heuristic. Add a response header X-Redwood-Resolution-Path that contains the path used (e.g., explicit->alias).

Backwards compatibility: do not change handler signatures. The marshalling envelope is only visible to internal handlers; for external outputs we rehydrate to the outward contract unless customer enables developer-preview headers to receive canonical metadata.

Fail-safe: if LCG is unavailable, runtime falls back to legacy heuristic used today and records a 'graph-miss' telemetry event. That fallback is limited to 1% of traffic per-customer while we validate.
Migration: provide a migration CLI tool that scans customer usage logs to propose alias mappings and suggests additions to LCG. Store suggestions as PRs to the manifest repo for manual review.
test_plan: Unit tests for resolution algorithm including exact/alias/sig/heuristic branches
Integration tests: end-to-end request with openai_tool metadata, legacy function payload, and ambiguous name to verify resolved canonical handler receives consistent envelope

Streaming tests: simulate partial text frames, incremental structured emission, and final frame validation. Verify client SDKs (JS/Python) can reassemble envelopes and return expected stream semantics
Chaos tests: LCG unavailability, manifest version skew, and simulated rate of collisions to validate metrics and fallback behavior
Performance tests: ensure marshalling adds <0.5ms median and <2ms p99 overhead for no-schema handlers; with schema validation enabled in canary expect additional cost but under SLO
Security tests: ensure envelope metadata doesn't leak internal alias tables to external responses; validate that debug headers require enterprise-entitlement
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): feature branch with runtime flag and unit/integration tests. Internal dogfood on staging cluster
Phase 1 (canary): enable for 5% of infra-team customers in us-west with manifest v1. Observe resolution metrics and schema violations for 72h
Phase 2 (broader canary): 25% traffic with automatic rollback on violation-rate > 0.2% or p50 latency regression > 10%
Phase 3 (gradual): per-customer opt-in using console toggle; provide migration suggestions to PMs and SEs
Phase 4: GA: flip default for new customers, existing customers on request; document manifest format and maintenance process
telemetry_and_alerting: Metrics: rdx.tool_resolve_total{path=...}, rdx.tool_resolve_failure_total, rdx.tool_collision_count, rdx.stream_schema_violation_total, rdx.resolution_latency_ms_p50_p95_p99
Logs: structured event with fields {request_id, original_name, canonical_name, resolution_path, invocation_origin, handler_id, outcome}
Alerts: high collision rate (>0.5% traffic) by tenant, schema violation spikes (>0.1% in canary), resolution-failure rate >0.2%
Dashboards: per-region/tenant breakdown, name alias churn over time, and top ambiguous names
risks_and_tradeoffs: Adding LCG increases operational complexity — manifests must be curated. We'll mitigate with tooling (suggested mappings) and RBAC on manifest edits
Heuristic matching can produce surprising resolution; heuristics are gated and will be retired after 4 weeks of monitoring
Schema validation on path increases CPU — initially run only in canary; GA will expose opt-in flags per-handler
Exposing too much metadata in responses risks customer confusion; keep canonical metadata internal unless developer-preview is requested
